newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ROYALS HOMER TWICE IN BOTTOM OF NINTH TO BEAT TIGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ROYALS HOMER TWICE IN BOTTOM OF NINTH TO BEAT TIGERS.

text.p: Mike Sweeney's two-run homer in the bottom of the ninth inning gave the Kansas City Royals their third straight win, 10-9 over the Detroit Tigers Thursday.

Pinch-hitter Johnny Damon led off the ninth with a homer off reliever Doug Brocail (0-4) to get the Royals within 9-8. Pinch-hitter Scott Cooper singled and Sweeney, who had entered the game in the eighth, followed with his second homer of the year on Brocail's 1-0 pitch.

"When I went up to the plate, I went up with the idea of bunting," Sweeney said. "I looked down at (third base coach) Rich Dauer and he gave the sign to swing away. I got an adrenaline rush. I got one crack at swinging."

Jamie Walker (2-1) earned the victory for the Royals, who won for the first time in 16 games this season when trailing after eight innings. Walker worked 1 1/3 scoreless innings and hasn't allowed a run in his last four appearances.
"My job as a pitcher is to get people out," Walker said. "I just wanted to stop them there and I did. That's just basically my job is to put up a zero."
Tony Clark and Melvin Nieves homered for Detroit.
Kansas City starter Kevin Appier was shelled for six runs and four hits in five innings. It matched his Opening Day start for his shortest of the year.
"It wasn't real pretty but it was a great ballgame," Kansas City manager Bob Boone said. "The dramatics of the ninth speak for themselves. We got Ape off the hook. We're going pretty good right now."

At Texas, Cecil Fielder belted a three-run homer in the first inning and Tim Raines added a two-run double in the sixth as the surging New York Yankees posted their fifth straight win, 8-2 over the Rangers.

The Yankees wasted little time in getting to Texas starter Jose Alberro (0-1) in the first inning. Alberro retired the first two batters but issued consecutive walks to Bernie Williams and Tino Martinez before Fielder launched his third home run of the season for a 3-0 lead.
Alberro left the game after the homer with muscle spasms in his lower back and was replaced by Matt Whiteside.
The Yankees have homered in 11 straight games.
New York broke open the game with four runs in the sixth, batting around for the 13th time this season.

Former Ranger Kenny Rogers (3-1) won for the first time in four starts, allowing two runs and nine hits over 6 1/3 innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out four. Jeff Nelson retired all five batters he faced and Brian Boehringer pitched a 1-2-3 ninth.
The Yankees, who have won eight of their last nine games, are 19-6 since opening the season 5-10.
Texas lost for the second time in seven games and has dropped all three meetings with New York this season. dropped three straight.
In Seattle, Chris Snopek's two-run double off closer Norm Charlton (2-2) with two out in the top of the ninth lifted the Chicago White Sox to a 4-3 victory over the Mariners.
It was Charlton's third blown save in 13 chances.
Bill Simas (1-0) recorded the final two outs in the eighth to pick up the win, while Roberto Hernandez worked a 1-2-3 ninth for his seventh save.
The White Sox had lost three games in a row and five straight on the road before winning in Seattle for just the fourth time in their last 14 tries.
Seattle's Ken Griffey Jr hit a two-run homer, his major-league leading 18th, in the first off Doug Drabek.

In Anaheim, Jason Dickson and four relievers combined on a three-hitter and Jack Howell had a pair of doubles and an RBI as the Angels handed the Baltimore Orioles their first losing series of the season with a 3-2 victory.

Dickson (6-1) allowed just two runs, including a homer to Rafael Palmeiro, over first seven innings. Chuck McElroy and Rich DeLucia combined for a scoreless eighth. Mike Holtz retired the first batter in the ninth before Mike James got the final two outs for his fifth save.
The Orioles were swept in the two-game series and fell to 25-13. Scott Kamieniecki (2-2) took the loss.
In Oakland, George Williams had a career-high three hits, including an RBI single that snapped an eighth-inning tie, as the Athletics edged the Milwaukee Brewers 6-5.
Patrick Lennon, brought up from the minors Wednesday, went 2-for-3 with a career-high three RBI for Oakland, which swept the two-game set after dropping its previous seven games.
Don Wengert (2-2), the fourth Athletics pitcher, worked two scoreless innings to earn the win. Bill Taylor got the final three outs for his eighth save.
Bob Wickman (2-2) took the loss.
